_comment: Accepted UNATTRIBUTED inert verdicts — fixtures whose attribute changed no pixels on the listed platforms and which no other ledger has an opinion about. This is the completeness ratchet behind `jui conformance gate --inert-complete`: an unattributed inert verdict that is NOT here fails the gate (an attribute can otherwise stop rendering and nothing says so), and an entry the measurement no longer supports fails too (a fixed attribute must not keep an excuse on file). Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the backlog — consume it by replacing the reason with the adjudication, or by fixing the platform and letting the entry go stale. An entry whose platform set changes returns to the backlog, because the adjudication was written about a different fact. Two optional keys carry the ruling in machine-readable form: 'adjudicatedFamily' is the family slug the reason prose also names, and 'controlDiffExclusion' — present only where the ruling removes the fixture from the control comparison — names the family justifying that removal. Consumers key off those, never off a sentinel inside the prose. Both are dropped when the platform set changes, for the same reason the verdict is.

adjudicated on the path the fixture actually renders through, AND a codegen/dynamic divergence worth F's attention. The ios conformance lane renders DYNAMIC, and SwiftJsonUI's IndicatorConverter.swift:33-34 returns EmptyView() whenever animating == false — it never reads hidesWhenStopped at all (no read site in that file). Control (stopped) and fixture (stopped, hidesWhenStopped:false) are therefore both empty and the inert verdict is structurally required. The CODEGEN path disagrees with that: sjui_tools indicator_converter.rb:19-30 defaults the attribute to true (matching UIKit) and, for the false face, keeps a zero-opacity spinner in the layout precisely so the surrounding layout still reflows — its own comment says that reflow is 'the whole reason the attribute exists'. So the two ios paths implement different rules for this spelling. Owner F: make the dynamic Indicator honour hidesWhenStopped:false the way codegen does. Even then this fixture cannot show it — the observable is a NEIGHBOUR being reflowed and the fixture has no neighbour (owner D). Family: reflow-only-observable.

adjudicated value-is-default, and it stays inert on both ios paths for two independent reasons. (1) The SSoT declares View.gradientDirection default "Vertical" and this fixture's control already carries the gradient, so the fixture restates the default; the codegen converter confirms it (sjui_tools modifier_helper.rb:16-23 has arms only for 'Horizontal'/'Oblique' and everything else, Vertical included, falls to the same top-to-bottom emit). (2) The path the fixture actually renders through is DYNAMIC, where a plain View's gradient is not applied at all — DynamicViewContainer.swift:105-108 casts rawData["gradient"] to [String: Any] while the SSoT types it as an array, and gradientDirection has no read site there.
